ev.t: Applies to: Primary, secondary, tertiary and transport packaging. Introduces minimization, labelling, recyclability, EPR and recycled-content rules; healthcare has targeted exemptions rather than a blanket exemption Date: Entered into force 11 February 2025; generally applicable from 12 August 2026

Applies to: Contact-sensitive pharmaceutical, MDR and IVDR plastic packaging. Exempts specified healthcare packaging from mandatory post-consumer recycled-content targets where safety and regulatory constraints apply Date: Application phased from 12 August 2026; recycled-content targets generally begin in 2030
Applies to: Contact-sensitive medical and pharmaceutical packaging. Delays 2030 design-for-recycling treatment for qualifying contact-sensitive packaging pending review Date: Review expected by 2035
ev.q: such packaging is exempt from the 2030 designed for recyclability mandate until a review in 2035.

ev.t: Applies to: Plastic containers, closures, glass containers and elastomeric closures. Establishes material and container tests, including pharmaceutical-use plastic requirements and extractables-related controls; a non-listed material may be accepted if justified and agreed by the authority Date: Current Ph. Eur. edition and applicable monograph dates

Applies to: Plastic components in direct contact with active substances or medicinal products. Requires identification, specifications, representative certificates of analysis and, where relevant, extraction and migration studies; does not state a universal virgin-resin requirement Date: Effective 1 December 2005

Applies to: Packaging systems for human drugs and biologics. Requires packaging suitability in protection, safety, compatibility and performance; packaging changes must be supported in the drug application Date: Final guidance issued May 1999; Q&A issued May 2002

Applies to: Post-consumer recycled plastic in primary drug-packaging components. Draft states that post-consumer recycled plastic should not be used in primary packaging components; draft guidance is nonbinding and not for implementation Date: Draft issued August 2026
ev.n: AI cross-check (ChatGPT): only partly supported. Given link opens a generic guidance search page, not the claimed document. The corrected August 2026 draft supports the claim and is expressly nonbinding/not for implementation. Verdict refers to supplied source. Link corrected.
ev.q: Postconsumer recycled plastic should not be used in the manufacture of a primary packaging component.
ev.w: Corrected PDF: printed p. 17 (PDF p. 21), section V.A.1, lines 528–529; cover and page headers

ev.t: Applies to: Plastic pharmaceutical packaging materials, components and systems. Provides standards for plastics used to package pharmaceuticals, biologics and dietary supplements; includes reference materials for HDPE, LDPE, PP and PET Date: Current USP–NF official date applies

Why it matters: Specialist programmes exist, but a regional denominator for total blister mass placed on the market and actually recovered is absent. Who needs it: Pharma companies, pharmacies, municipalities and EPR systems

ev.t: Why it matters: Laboratory separation of PVC, PVdC and aluminium does not establish commercial energy demand, solvent loss, cost or net environmental benefit. Who needs it: Recyclers, blister producers and LCA practitioners

evidence.statement: Autoclave followed by landfill or municipal treatment (Multiple regions). Quantity: GAP — no harmonized IVD-specific percentage. Barrier: Autoclaving disinfects but does not separate polymers or remove all chemical contamination
evidence.source: WHO healthcare-waste guidance

evidence.statement: Incineration, autoclaving, microwave treatment, chemical treatment or landfill after treatment (Global). Quantity: WHO classifies about 85% as non-hazardous and 15% as hazardous; this is not a treatment split. Barrier: Infectious, chemical, pharmaceutical and sharps risks require controlled treatment
evidence.source: WHO healthcare-waste fact sheet

evidence.statement: Incineration (Germany). Quantity: Study covered 103,432 tonnes from 122 hospital sites; 91% classified non-hazardous and 9% hazardous; almost all hospital-specific waste reported as incinerated. Barrier: Mixed hospital collection and strict hygiene management
evidence.source: Vielsack et al. 2026, Waste Management & Research

evidence.statement: Incineration (South Korea). Quantity: More than 90% reported as incinerated in certified facilities. Barrier: Medical-waste regulation and contamination
evidence.source: Medical-plastics study

evidence.statement: Incineration (United States). Quantity: Approximately 7% in a voluntary 2013 sample of 198 hospitals. Barrier: Sample not nationally representative; newer national split GAP
evidence.source: Healthcare-waste assessment

evidence.statement: High-temperature incineration (Multiple regions). Quantity: GAP. Barrier: Autoclaving does not neutralize many pharmaceutical, cytotoxic or chemical residues
evidence.source: WHO pharmaceutical-waste guidance

evidence.statement: Applies to: All waste, including non-excluded healthcare and packaging waste. Establishes the hierarchy of prevention, preparing for reuse, recycling, other recovery and disposal; also establishes polluter-pays and EPR principles Date: Entered into force 12 December 2008
evidence.source: Government summary

stages.src: Public EPD S-P-10470 (Billerud CrownBoard Prestige 285 g/m2), International EPD System, reference year 2024, GWP-fossil; 377 kg CO2e per tonne
